content.text: Fifty-one Japanese (Gojūichi / äº”å ä¸€) is a popular fast-paced children's and social card game in Japan. A variation of the 'Commerce' family of games, it focuses on suit-based point collection. Players interact with a public pool of five cards on the table, swapping their own cards to reach a target score of 51. The game is known for its tension-filled ending, where one player can 'Stop' the game, giving everyone else only one last chance to improve their hand.
Part of the global '51' family, which includes the Chinese Wǔshíyī Diǎn and various European variants. In Japan, it has transitioned from a gambling game into a staple family and childhood game.
Assign five cards to each player and place five cards face-up in the center of the table (the 'Market'). The remaining cards form the draw pile (used only when the table is cleared).
